findingDispositions.reason: Independently read packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts resolveGraphPackage and describeLocation: assetDir and vendorDir are derived from packageRoot inside the same function that locates the dist/index.js entry, and startServer consumes both fields every invocation. Confirmed packages/graph/package.json has only main and types fields, no exports map, so no alternate seam exists today for asset/vendor path resolution once the entry-file import is deleted. Risk is real and specific to work not yet started; concurs with concept lane.

Independently confirmed: root package.json has no workspaces field; package-lock.json lockfileVersion 3 has zero entries for packages/main, packages/utils, or packages/graph as local packages. packages/main/node_modules/@lattice/lab is a manual symlink pointing to ../../../lab sitting inside gitignored node_modules, not reproduced by npm install, and grep confirms @lattice/lab is not statically imported anywhere in packages/main/src. Reverse case @proof-or-stop/core in packages/utils/package.json fails require.resolve. The cited precedent is genuinely unproven; concurs with quality lane.

Independently confirmed both structural claims against current code: root package.json build script runs packages/main before packages/graph, so packages/graph/dist would not exist yet for a static import from main to resolve or type-check; and packages/graph/src/index.ts statically re-exports search from core/search/fn.js, which has a top-level import of DatabaseSync from node:sqlite -- a static import in handlers/graph.ts would hoist that load out of the current on-demand guarded path, since assertGraphRuntimeSupported runs strictly before the existing dynamic import per the load-bearing comment in graph.ts. Confirmed real regression risk in work not yet done; concurs with quality lane. Noted for the record and not part of this disposition: the user has since directed the fix to include splitting node:sqlite out of the eager re-export chain specifically to prevent this regression.

Independently reproduced from scratch in an isolated tmp copy of the full worktree, separate from the docs lane's own artifacts: positive control on unmodified process-fact-levels.ts passes cleanly with Process fact contract verified exit 0; after removing the graph entry and rerunning verify-process-fact-contract.mjs quiet, the failure output contains exactly nine distinct complaint lines, one MAIN_TOOLS missing from registry, seven DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS phase allowlist drift lines one per phase DEV DONE INIT INIT_CHECK PLAN REVIEW TEST, and one MAIN_TOOLS command missing from PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY; restoring the entry returns to a clean pass. The decision doc text says eight. My own independent reproduction confirms nine, matching the docs lane; concurs with docs lane.

Independently inspected proof-or-stop.config.json validate.commands, 113 entries with no match for surface or ownership as bare npm-script invocations, and root package.json test:serial-reference: cli-surface-smoke and verify-orphan-surface are absent from both, existing only as standalone npm run scripts. By contrast confirmed command-ownership-contract IS transitively covered: red-evidence-target-binding-smoke.ts, which is in validate.commands, internally invokes command-ownership-contract.js as a sub-check. This story's own CHK-003 verification evidence had to invoke test:orphan-surface manually, corroborating that nothing re-runs it automatically. Concurs with docs lane.

Independently confirmed both cited passages currently exist verbatim as described: packages/graph/README.md How the CLI reaches this package section states the handler resolves the package at RUNTIME rather than importing it statically because packages/graph is not a dependency of packages/main; packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts MODULE RESOLUTION header comment gives the same rationale. Both would become false once the package becomes a file dependency with a static import, per the user's stated fix direction. Correctly scoped as advisory forward-risk, not a defect in the current merged tree; concurs with docs lane.

Independently confirmed cli-surface-smoke and verify-orphan-surface are absent from proof-or-stop.config.json validate.commands and root package.json test:serial-reference (same grep result as F-012), and independently confirmed checklist.json CHK-003 userSees names exactly these two plus command-ownership-contract and command-catalog-smoke as acceptance evidence. The distinguishing claim beyond F-012 -- that this story's OWN acceptance criteria cites unwired guards as evidence, making it a concept-completeness defect in this story's deliverable rather than a general doc-accuracy complaint -- is independently verified and correctly scoped as a separate, non-duplicate family from F-012 (see F-012 reasoning for why they do not auto-cluster).

Independently read packages/graph/README.md and the graph.ts MODULE RESOLUTION header: both currently give only the removable reason (no workspaces / not a declared dependency) for the dynamic import, and neither states the binding reason (node:sqlite is unavoidably reachable through any static import chain into the graph library, per F-010's independently-confirmed empirical finding on Node v20.19.6). Confirmed the decisions doc frames itself as recording exactly this class of non-obvious rationale. This finding's recommendation is now more urgent, not less, given the plan explicitly keeps the dynamic import permanently rather than as a temporary stopgap -- if the binding reason is never written down, a future contributor who adds packages/graph as a dependency has no documented reason not to also convert the import to static, silently reintroducing the F-010 regression. Concurs with docs lane.

Independently read isKnownBenignNonLiteralLoaderCall in retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts: it checks only (a) the whole-file AST fingerprint matches the pinned digest and (b) the enclosing function name plus the call's first-argument TEXT matches an approved {anchor,argument} pair. It performs no check on the argument's underlying data-flow provenance (e.g., that location.entry still traces only to resolveGraphPackage()/packageRoot rather than becoming caller-influenced) -- confirmed by reading the full function body and its call sites at lines ~1537-1548. The mechanism proves 'the file has not changed since approval', not 'the approved narrow shape still holds after a semantically-different edit that preserves the same textual anchor/argument shape'. This is a real, currently-unaddressed mechanical gap that would also apply, with equal force, to the planned graph-runtime.ts extraction itself: extracting the loader into a smaller file does not add a provenance check, it only shrinks the blast radius of what a whole-file fingerprint pins -- the underlying reliance on human-written re-approval-basis comments (rather than a mechanical assertion) is unchanged by the extraction. Concurs with test-coverage lane and extends its relevance to the planned remediation.

Independently traced the same chain: cli-engine.ts strips a global --root flag into rootOverride, cli/runtime-root.ts resolveRoot returns it verbatim with no sanitization for any command other than story_discard, and ctx.root reaches resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root) in graph.ts. Independently confirmed the existing precedent this finding cites -- verifier/serve.ts startCircuitServe is already in the same knownBenignNonLiteralLoaderCalls allowlist and walks a --root-derived directory to dynamically import whatever machine.ts it finds -- so the trust model genuinely already exists and graph.ts extends rather than introduces it. Independently confirmed the dual-map maintenance cost claim: knownBenignNonLiteralLoaderCalls/BENIGN_NON_LITERAL_LOADER_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS and DYNAMIC_CODE_GENERATION_FINGERPRINT_EXEMPTIONS are two separate maps in the same file, both pinning whole-file digests, so a single future edit to graph.ts (or to a would-be graph-runtime.ts) needs two coordinated re-pins -- consistent with the existing bin/bootstrap-runner.js entries in both maps, which is real precedent for this being an ongoing, not one-time, maintenance cost. Concurs with quality lane; this is the wave's strongest finding because it is the only one that surfaced a security property (attacker-controlled --root reaching a live dynamic import with zero markers required) that none of the other three lanes, nor the wave-1 critic, examined.
